name: Fall of Singapore
note: The plan shows the whole operation on the island, 8 to 13 February 1942, not a single field: each block is a brigade, division or corps. The accounts place the formations by sector, not by exact position, so the blocks stand roughly where their sectors lay, and the coastline is only sketched.

phases.title: The island divided into three sectors
phases.text: Two Australian brigades held the west, where the invasion was most likely, III Indian Corps held the north-east and the Southern Area forces the south-east. The Japanese stood across the Johor Strait.
phases.quote: Percival gave Major-General Gordon Bennett's two brigades from the 8th Australian Division responsibility for the western side of Singapore

phases.title: The 5th and 18th Divisions land in the north-west
phases.text: The first wave crossed the strait shortly before 20:30. The main weight, about 13,000 men, fell on the 22nd Australian Brigade, which numbered just 3,000.
phases.quote: The main weight of the Japanese force, about 13,000 men, from 16 assault battalions, with five in reserve, attacked the 22nd Australian Brigade.

phases.title: The 22nd Brigade falls back towards the centre
phases.text: The Australian battalions that had been engaged regrouped and moved back east from the coast, and the Japanese divisions followed inland. The Australians were pushed back further in the early morning.
phases.quote: the three Australian battalions that had been engaged sought to regroup, moving back east from the coast towards the centre of the island, which was completed mainly in good order

phases.title: The Imperial Guards attack the 27th Brigade
phases.text: The Guards crossed on the 27th Brigade's front, near the causeway, and some reached the shore. Mortars, machine-guns and burning oil on the water caused them severe casualties, and Yamashita ordered them to press on.
phases.quote: Late on 9 February, the Imperial Guards began assaulting the positions held by the 27th Brigade, concentrating on those held by the 2/26th Battalion.

phases.title: The 27th Brigade withdraws from the causeway
phases.text: Maxwell could not contact the 22nd Brigade and feared encirclement. His brigade withdrew east of the Bukit Timah Road, and the Allies lost the beaches by the causeway. Bennett later said he had not authorised the move.
phases.quote: the 2/26th Battalion was forced to withdraw to a position east of the Bukit Timah Road

phases.title: The Japanese push on to Bukit Panjang and Bukit Timah
phases.text: The 5th Division aimed at Bukit Panjang and the 18th Division at Bukit Timah. The 18th fell on the 22nd Brigade's area, and the Japanese captured the Bukit Timah area with the garrison's main food and fuel depots.
phases.quote: the 5th Division aimed its advance towards Bukit Panjang, while the 18th Division struck out towards Bukit Timah

phases.title: The Commonwealth forces pull back to a city perimeter
phases.text: The Commonwealth forces withdrew from the northern shore and Changi to a perimeter around Singapore City at the eastern end of the island, with harassing attacks all the way. The 44th Brigade held from Buona Vista to Pasir Panjang.
phases.quote: the order was given for a 28 mi (45 km) perimeter to be established around Singapore City at the eastern end of the island
